clue.text: Mother blocking change in old school, say

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in the middle of it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to change something is to alter it
mama is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother stands in the way of reforms at a traditional school.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the Latin-derived term for the school or university a person once attended; 'say' marks school as one example.

clue.text: Too dismal, sordid houses

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer, holding it inside its own letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A grim, squalid set of houses is described as depressing too.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both meaning in addition.

clue.text: Souvenir of chaps in feminist movement briefly

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped
one item placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: MeToo is the campaign against sexual harassment
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A keepsake recalling the men caught up in the MeToo movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder, which is what a souvenir is.

clue.text: Perhaps bishop's staff

blocks.note: first meaning: a chess piece, of which the bishop is one example
second meaning: to provide workers for, as in to crew a post

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bishop's crook or his employees; in fact the bishop is a chess piece, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and as a verb the word means to supply people to work at a station.

clue.text: Argument about a right price

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the others

blocks.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over whether a charge is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a fixed charge or schedule of charges, so it serves as a price.

clue.text: Stories from Dumas père and fils or Martin and Kingsley Amis?

definitions.text: Dumas père and fils or Martin and Kingsley Amis?
definitions.note: the pairs are examples, hence the question mark

blocks.note: first meaning: narratives or accounts, as in the relation of a tale

blocks.clueFragment: Dumas père and fils or Martin and Kingsley Amis?
blocks.note: second meaning: kin, here two father-and-son pairs of novelists

explanation.walkthrough: Both pairs of writers are father and son, so the surface looking for literary works is a trap: the second sense is family members.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a recounted story, and relations are also relatives such as fathers and sons.

clue.text: Small, silver sink

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A little silver kitchen basin.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or subside downward, which is to sink.

clue.text: Clean vessel with king aboard

indicators.note: someone aboard a vessel is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles

explanation.surface: The crew scrub down a ship ahead of a royal visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to clean something by rubbing hard.

clue.text: They keep people locked up and glare so awfully

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Prison guards lock inmates away and scowl at them fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaolers, the British spelling of jailers, are prison warders who keep inmates confined.

clue.text: Class remains disorganised

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A lesson that stays chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small teaching session at a university, a kind of class.

clue.text: Mythical ship, on lake, proceeding slowly

indicators.note: one thing written on another in an across clue comes after it, so the ship follows the lake

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: Jason's ship drifts slowly across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning at a slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Change of a blueprint struggling commercially

indicators.note: a change of something alters it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A firm revises its business plan because it is failing to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that is unprofitable makes no money, so it is struggling in trade.

clue.text: Check transport during time off work

indicators.note: something during a period falls within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a rest is a break from work
a train is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Someone checks the train timetable while on holiday.

clue.text: Playing boules in female attire

indicators.note: letters at play are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A woman plays boules dressed in her finery.

clue.text: What Oasis made, having drained beer, vermouth and soft drink

indicators.note: a drained word has had its contents emptied, leaving only its shell

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
pop is fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: The band Oasis knocking back beer, vermouth and lemonade.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis is the 1990s Manchester band, not a desert spring; 'gin and it' is a British name for gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was the 1990s British guitar-music movement of which Oasis were leading exponents.

clue.text: Manages to carry you, we hear, in cars

to carry something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

the letter U is pronounced like this word

explanation.definitionFit: Coupés are two-door cars with a fixed roof, so they are a kind of car.

clue.text: Skill shown by journalists drinking old whiskey

clue.text: Ancient poet runs wearing watch

explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid, so he is a poet of antiquity.

clue.text: Italian team needing goal and break in play, say

blocks.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
a mission is an aim or goal

explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is the interval in a play or film; 'say' marks a play as one example.

clue.text: Hint sentry's outside, slightly sozzled

the first and last letters of the word

clue.text: Crossword setters and our boss getting employed

clue.text: One's energy returns, getting fizzy drink

taken as written

clue.text: Runners of errands welcoming learner drivers, perhaps?

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers use the club called a driver to tee off, so they can be called drivers.

clue.text: Algarve oddly ignored for convenience

clue.text: Secretary getting unknown remuneration
